segment.source: ::He is focused on packing.::<end>

Æterbæren!
::The man swiftly grabs his spear and assumes a fighting stance.::<end>
::Show him your open palms and try to act as nonthreatening as possible.::<end>
::Your peaceful actions do not seem to have the desired effect: ::<end>
::He advances forward, skillfully maintaining his stance and keeping himself well behind the deadly tip of his spear which is now, in turn, getting dangerously close to your own body.::<end>
Forskar Flotsourmir!<end>

::The name roots him in place. It does not disarm the man - the spear tip still hovers before you - but instead makes him echo the name, uttering it with great respect and pride.::
Forskarr Flottsørmir.<end>
Forskarr Flotsourmir!<end>

::He echoes it again, louder and fiercer.::
Forskarr Flottsørmir!<end>
Forskarr Flotsourmir!<end>
Dur... hruknepönen ot meltønge lætta?<end>
::Shrug your shoulders.::<end>

::He briefly inspects you, his eyes mostly focused on your upper body.::
Dur nikkt vertään det saperønt ot Firg, met Flottsørmir Dur forskarren. Polløknæ...<end>

::You both stare at each other motionlessly. As the atmosphere begins to cool down, you notice a pleasant smell of crab meat being cooked over a steady, calm fire; the sight of it glimmering so succulently is as inviting as the host wasn't during the first moments of your encounter. But even that seems to be changing: The man slowly crouches next to the fire, places his spear at his feet and checks the tender meat. He is still quite cautious of you but seems at ease enough that you may attempt to approach him.::<end>
::Pat your chest.:: $(context.player.Name). ::Then point your finger at him.::<end>
::He observes you with an expressionless countenance.::<end>
::Pat your chest again.:: $(context.player.Name). Me. ::Point at him.:: You...?<end>
::He hesitates...::<end>

::...but then places his hand on his chest and imitates your gesture.::
Yngwar.<end>
Ik - Yngwar. Dur - $(context.player.Name).<end>

::He returns to his work, producing a few skewers made of bone from the leather sack next to him. He seems focused on food preparation, but he's indubitably aware of everything you do. He removes the cooked meat from the fire and replaces it with fresh skewers.::<end>
::Approach him and stand by the fire with him.::<end>
::He shows no objection to you approaching him.::<end>
<end>
About Sjörsr...<end>
::He nods.::<end>
<end>
Where was he hit, again? ::Gesture something piercing your flesh.::<end>
::He observes you for a moment...::<end>
::Then shows the point of impact on himself: He was hit in his $(GiantSkerderHitBodyPart_DisplayName).::<end>
What happened to his body? ::Gesture it as best as you can.::<end>
::He draws water, then the ground, then huge, towering bones sticking out. Above it, he draws a rune of some kind.::<end>
<end>
::Point to the rune, then gesture scribbling.:: Can you write that down for me?<end>
::He doesn't seem to understand but draws the rune deeper.::<end>
::Point to a piece of leather lying on the ground next to his sack.:: Can I have that? Can, uh, Ik, I don't know, tekken that?<end>

::He nods and takes the leather. But instead of giving it to you, he first burns the end of one of the skewers in the fire and then uses it to write the rune into the leather. Then he hands it to you.::
Sjörsr akkøsska firt bryjäällen ot ponne bitt.<end>
Never mind.<end>
::Inquire about something else.::<end>
::He is silent.::<end>
What does it mean?<end>
::He explains no further but tends to his fire instead.::<end>
::Nod and change the subject.::<end>
::He tends to his fire in silence.::<end>
::He points to his drawing of huge, towering bones sticking out. Above it, there is a rune of some kind.::<end>
About Sjoersr...<end>
Yngwar... <end>
Jakke...<end>
You are different from your brethren, the Sørmirbæren. Durg, um... bitt... um...<end>
Ik mætäre: Ik ænnerfe bitt.<end>
Jakke. Durg ænnerfen bitt. The rituals, the, um... the shapes you saw in the light... Lysbørggamen.<end>

::He nods.:: Ik mætäre.
::He draws the symbol of Flottsørmir in the sand with his trusty bone knife.::<end>

::There is no doubt that He is the Serpent, that He is the Father who gave them their strength, skill and bloodthirst. He gave them this sea to be their homeland and its many inhabitants to slay. But the Way the spiriters want Yngwar to follow is wrong.
He understands that now.::<end>

Durg Æterbæren bitt...
::You may or may not understand. That is not important to Yngwar.::<end>
Hvæy Durg... uh, vertään er kæ Merg? Why tell me all of that, then?<end>
::By trying to explain to an Otherborn the things that troubled him he understood them better himself. He understood them well enough. Now he knows what he must do.::<end>

::There is another way, the Way of the Warrior, the Way of Man, where eyes do not have to be blinded to see, where limbs do not have to be shed away to be strong. Because Yngwar can be much stronger as Flottsørmir's warrior than as Flottsørmir's serpent.::
Det Krigsfarvääj - vääj ot det lemann.<end>
::An old, weak sailor slew Flottsørmir's greatest warrior with a tiny glowing rock. Yngwar must go to its "source," the glow itself and begin his Way there.::<end>
<end>
You're going to the monolith? ::Point southeast.::<end>
::The word "monolith" seems to confuse him temporarily, but he still nods in affirmation.::<end>
::Tell him about what you saw in the monolith's vision.::<end>
::He expressionlessly waits for you to say something.::<end>
::Try to explain to him the things you saw: the traveler, the king, the two shafts of pure light...::<end>

::He follows your narrative with acute attention, interpreting the discrepancies between his and your conception as to receive as much information as possible. The traveler, the light, the falling king - it all seems to make sense to him.::<end>
::He raises his spear just as you were about to get to the part with the burning light, implicitly taking on the role of the traveler.::<end>
::He lowers the spear, looks at you and nods, pleased and proud.::<end>
::Try to explain to him the few things you saw: the slithering serpent, the crown upon the stone...::<end>
::He pauses. You get the feeling he understood most of what you were trying to communicate, but your words leave him pondering.::<end>

::He raises his head and responds.::
<end>
Det Krigsfarvääj Ik møsst trekke.<end>
::Explain to him that you saw blinding fires burning all warriors who dare approach it - for eternity.::<end>

::He is focused on your narrative and quickly shows signs of dissatisfaction.::
Krökø! Durg höppælysk gørren Merg!<end>

::Distrust grows in his eyes because things don't make sense to him. He senses your deception and responds by grabbing his spear...::
<end>
::Fight!::<end>
::Say nothing.::<end>
::He remains expressionless.::<end>
You aren't afraid that the Lysbørggamen might kill you?<end>
::He shakes his head.:: Ik ænnerfe bitt.<end>
There is another monolith, deep below the surface of the sea.<end>
Ænnerfen grønt stänn? Hvær er bitt?<end>
It's in, um... *Abyssal* Station. ::Point down, deep, deep down, and explain to him what you experienced as best as you can.::<end>

::He's captivated by your story, trying his best to understand every word and every gesture you utter and make. The very existence of this underwater place and how you reached it via a "floating shell," it fascinates him so much, but the moment you mention the Shadowlith... his attention turns into something else, something more - recognition.::
Det Mørrstänn!<end>

::The Black Rock - in the Temple of the Tides. It's the same thing you're describing, the only difference being their relative sizes: The rock beneath the sea is larger than a man - a transcended even; the rock in the Temple is small, yet it's as heavy as a thousand rocks.
The spiriters use this relic for various rituals and enchantments; they mind-speak with it - and they say it speaks back in His tongue.::<end>

::He works out that the two rocks were one even before you got to mention the missing piece from the top of the Shadowlith - you could see it clearly in his eyes - and the darkening effect - he recognizes it just the same. The gloom beyond the windows, the opening portals, the serpentine void creatures, these he finds hard to interpret properly, but he *feels* the essence of what you experienced. Yet somehow it remains unclear whether he interprets it to be reality as you understand it, or something one would experience in a ritualistic trance, or even something else entirely.
In any case, you end your story with the submarine's ascent.::<end>

::After some thinking he relays his thoughts briefly: Had he heard this earlier in his life, it would reinforce his faith in the Way of the spiriters - for this Black Rock would be the supreme source of His immense influence, lying deep in His underwater realm, waiting for the transcended ones to swim to it. But now that he recognizes the connection between the two Great Rocks and the two Ways, and that the Black Rock's "glow" is to the spiriters what Lysbørggamen is to him, he understands even more why he must follow a different Way.::
Det Krigsfarvääj - vääj ot det lemann! ::He repeats resolutely.::<end>
How will you leave? ::Gesture a boat sailing away.::<end>
::His eyes trace the surrounding walls all the way to the ceiling. Then he raises his hands...::<end>
::...and mimics climbing.::<end>
::Take a step back.:: Then go.<end>

::He looks at his things and begins counting them using his phalanges, doing so in groups of six, as before. Once he reaches his other, deformed hand you notice something odd - his index finger on that hand has four phalanges, making that the only grouping wherein he has counted seven items.
It makes you wonder for a few moments, and then...::<end>
::He sits by the fire and begins pulling things out of a leather sack.::<end>
::Wait and see what he does.::<end>

::He grabs a stone mortar, a bone pestle, a bag of white pearls and a reed brush. He crushes the pearls into fine powder, pours in some water from one waterskin and some sticky, honey-like substance from another, smaller one. He then pours everything into a thin bowl and heats it over the fire, mixing it until its consistency turns thick.::<end>

::The warpaint is ready, and after waiting for it to cool off a bit he applies it to his face, smearing his skin with his hands, but the scales he treats with the reed brush.
Now he's ready.::<end>
Good luck, Yngwar. ::Leave.::<end>
::Just leave.::<end>
I cannot let you kill in Flottsørmir's name, savage! ::Attack!::<end>
Well, screw you too.<end>
::He raises his hand.::<end>
::Observe him.::<end>

::Now that you don't have to worry about him driving his spear between your eyes you can use the aforementioned to observe him at leisure. For instance, only now do you notice that his left forearm and hand are larger and of less regular shape than his right: The fingers are thicker and somewhat crooked at the joints - making them less dexterous when doing fine, precise work, such as putting meat on or turning the skewers - and the scales on that arm almost form a sturdy, reptilian gauntlet; almost - as there are a few patches of exposed purple-red flesh.::<end>

::There are many other details you notice: the tattoo on his chest - the same one you keep seeing around - the numerous bony piercings, the quality leather belt and backpack strap, the loincloth made of a material much finer and oddly more elegant than the simple furry greaves he's wearing.::<end>

::[Perception] There is, in fact, plenty of visual conflict in his appearance: For each of his serpentine features there is an opposing humanizing one, like the way his scales grow around, and therefore emphasize, his biceps - perhaps the most recognizable symbol of male strength - or the difference between his cruder, malforming hand and his accurate, if scale-covered normal one.
Even the dominant, curved lines of the tattoo are but boxed into the outlinear matrix of his pectoral and abdominal muscles.::<end>
::As you finish examining him, so does he finish examining you.::<end>
::Point at him.:: Yngwar.<end>
::He is silent.::<end>

Uh... ::Pat your chest.::
$(context.player.Name) - brave. ::Look brave as best as you can.::
$(context.player.Name) - smart. ::Tap your head and hope he gets it.::
$(context.player.Name) - adventurer. ::Use two fingers to imitate a person's legs.:: <end>

::A moment passes.::
$(context.player.Name)...<end>

Æterbæren. Dur Æterbæren.
Yngwar - Sørmirbæren.
Yngwar - Skærder.
Yngwar - trekker... ::He mimics your walking fingers.::<end>

::He picks up his knife, a blade made of bone and painted with blood, and approaches the sand. He starts by drawing waves, then ground above it. Tents soon emerge, people and livestock follow. He draws a doming cavern above it all, and places himself to the left, where the dome meets the water, far away from his tribe. He rests the knife's point on the drawn version of himself and says...::
Yngwar. Yngwar. ::He pats his chest.::<end>
$(context.player.Name). ::He points to you, then the sand.::<end>
<end>
::Draw South Gate Station.::<end>

::You pick up a small sharp bone and start drawing the floors of South Gate Station, one by one, starting with the lowest one. As the floors multiply, so do the details that give the drawing some character: the shooting range, the bar, the hopper pen...
The last inhabitant you draw is a hunchbacked stick figure standing outside the lowest floor.::<end>
::He observes your drawing with curiosity before adding a wave just below the ground floor, making it look as though most of the station is underwater.::<end>
::Draw the Institute of Tchort.::<end>

::You pick up a small sharp bone and draw a large eye from which tentacles emerge - the entrance to the Institute. You then proceed to draw its layout, connecting the squares which represent floors and rooms with stairs and long hallways. The numerous vases also help to embellish the drawing. ::<end>
::And then, a large number of stick figures arrive and kill everyone.::<end>

::The onslaught disturbs him slightly, but not for the expected reasons, it seems. He points to the tentacles a few times, their slithery nature obviously provoking great interest in him. He shakes his head and speaks.::
Tirg sørmiren zöne Tir krigsppæt nikkt. Nikkt. Tir Dødten bitt, husse.<end>
That is Tchort you're pointing at. Tchort. Tchort.<end>
Tchort. Tchort...<end>

Fir... ::He pats his chest.:: Forskarr Flottsørmir! Tir... ::He points to the stick Tchortists.:: Forskarr Tchort. Fir - Sørmirbæren. Tir - Tchortbæren. Jakke.
Met Flottsørmir... möktter! Möktter!<end>
Forskarr Flottsørmir!<end>
No. No Flotsourmir - Tchort!<end>
Tchort? ::He spits at you.:: Forskarr Flottsørmir! ::He shoves you away and grabs his spear.::<end>
Forskar Flotsourmir.<end>
::He looks at the drawing some more, ::<end>
::then turns around to check his crab meat.::<end>
::Say nothing.::<end>
<end>

::He points to the tentacles a few times, their slithery nature obviously provoking great interest in him.::
Flottsørmir? Ik se nikkt jørre aut.<end>
No, that is Tchort. Tchort.<end>
::Draw the expedition camp.::<end>
::You pick up a small sharp bone and start by drawing the many tents in the camp, and then eclipse them all with a tall lighthouse::<end>
::atop which a lone figure stands. ::<end>
::You add jet skis patrolling around it, sec-troopers fighting sea serpents, laborers carrying boxes and Chief Briggs yelling at Ladelman.::<end>

::He observes your drawing with curiosity, but you notice that he does not recognize the camp. He nods a few times and adds a few tribal details to your tents.::
Jakke... Tyrten gøttæ aule päkke-päkke.<end>
::Draw the Free Drones base.::<end>

::You pick up a small sharp bone and start by drawing the railway. Then you draw a network of tunnels underneath it. And then you cram an entire community of stick figures in a few small rooms, with Hutch and Laser guarding the entrance.::<end>

::He observes your drawing with curiosity, then points at Laser.::
Mø? ::He then starts mooing.:: Mø?<end>
Um, yes. Mu.<end>
::He moos one more time, ::<end>
No. Woof-woof.<end>
Woof-woof...? Bau-bau? ::He barks like a dog as his gaze turns southeast.::<end>
Yes. Bau-bau.<end>
::He barks one more time, ::<end>
Not bau-bau - woof-woof!<end>
Bau-bau!<end>
::Draw Fort Apogee.::<end>

::You pick up a small sharp bone and start by drawing a large courtyard where stick figures stand in ranks. You then proceed to draw the layout of the base, the barracks, the repair bay, consulate and, of course, the boxing ring. And you do not forget to draw a large robot at the entrance.::<end>

::He observes your drawing with curiosity, then points at the Dreadnought.::
Dänn... aen truppal skærder. Jakke! ::Its drill-arm seems to interest him the most.:: Et grønt bitt! <end>
::Draw Port Ceto.::<end>

::You use your finger to draw waves, then on them a large ship surrounded by platforms. You protect them with high walls and within them add stick figures of different shapes and sizes; the smallest one is surrounded by three lady stick figures. On the outside you add patrolling jetters, and that provokes a reaction from Yngwar...::<end>
::He shoves you away with his enlarged hand while grabbing his spear with the other.::<end>
::Draw railroad tracks and empty roads.::<end>

::You use your finger to draw a network of interweaving roads and railways. You draw gangs, dogs and rathounds - the last two with little difference - inhabiting these, and then you add moving trains and broken down quad bikes.::<end>

::He observes your drawing with curiosity, then points at the railway.::
Bæn... trekkergar jömt mitt bæn. ::He picks up a few bones and places them parallel to one another, just like rail ties. He finds this interesting.:: Bæntrekkergar.<end>
::Draw the sea.::<end>
::You use your finger to draw waves before finishing the drawing by adding a small boat.::<end>
::He observes your drawing with curiosity, then draws a man on the boat, and some kind of smoke following him. ::<end>
::Shake your head.::<end>
::He points to you again, then at the sand.::<end>
<end>

::He spits on the ground and waves you away, following it with some unintelligible cursing.::
Trekkenørgen... Trekkenørgen!<end>
What?<end>
::He grabs his spear.::<end>
I get it. ::Leave.::<end>
::Leave without saying a word.::<end>
::Attack!::<end>
::Do nothing.::<end>
::Point at his arm, or more specifically its scaly skin.::<end>
::He inspects you, then starts touching your clothes.::<end>
::Push him away.:: Outta my space.<end>
::He responds by shoving you back. ::<end>
<end>
::Say nothing, just stare at him.::<end>
::He looks at you for a moment, then ::<end>
::returns to attending his fireplace.::<end>
Watch it!<end>
::Slap his hand aside.:: Don't touch me!<end>
::He grabs your arm mid-air and shoves you away. ::<end>
::Step away from him.:: No.<end>
::He too steps back.:: <end>
Dänn Rætter bitt. Grønt rætter... Hvær Dur ykdrääsil kær grønt rætten?<end>
::[Intelligence] It's the regalia. Something about it fascinates him.::<end>
Rætter. ::He points to your regalia.:: Rætter. Grønt! ::He gestures something large.::<end>
::[Intelligence] It's the regalia. Perhaps he's never seen a rathound before.:: Reter, yes. Big reters in Underrail. ::Gesture how big.::<end>

Rætterheund?
Ønderr-räyl...<end>
<end>
There rats big. Not good for nom nom. ::Mimic eating and make a sour face..:: But good for clothes. ::Appear comfortable in your regalia.::<end>
::He finds your explanation amusing and points at his loincloth, making himself look rather comfy as well.::<end>
::He inspects the regalia for a few more moments, then ::<end>
There rats big. Good for nom nom. ::Mimic eating and make a pleased face..:: But better for clothes. ::Appear comfortable in your regalia.::<end>
Yes.<end>
::Nod and leave it at that.::<end>
Rathound?<end>
Rættenheund?<end>
Yes. Big rats from Underrail.<end>
Ønderr-räyl...<end>
I don't get it.<end>
::He shakes his head, looks at the regalia some more, then ::<end>
::Shrug your shoulders.::<end>
::[Intelligence] It's the regalia. Perhaps he's never seen a rathound before.:: Not reter - reterhound. Big retenhounds in Underrail. ::Gesture how big.::<end>
What?<end>
::Shrug your shoulders.::<end>
::Let him keep touching you.::<end>
Hvarga? <end>
<end>
::He grabs his bone knife...::<end>
::...and begins drawing in the sand. This in combination with his gesturing and an occassional sentence forms a narrative you try your best to follow.::<end>
::[Intelligence] Observe and listen.::<end>

::His tale begins with the difference between the two skins: One you are born with, the other you earn. Not everyone can earn it, no, as not everyone is strong enough - not everyone has been destined to achieve transcendence. "Abyssal" transcendence, it seems, for he looks down and points his hands to the ground, his palms being fully open.::
Skærden... Forskarr Flottsørmir! Forskarr Pöm.<end>

::Men who relay Flotsourmir's messages organize some kind of ritualistic drinking of a "potion of serpent essence." It drops men to the ground and makes them convulse like serpents in pain. It burns from below and outside but later they feel that very serpentine essence imbuing them. Weaklings die. The strong will begin or continue their transformation.
But then he speaks of further rituals: They all begin with the consumption of these potions, but each one is followed by new challenges. And then he abruptly stops.::<end>

::He starts by showing you the difference between the two skins, but you gain no new information. It seems that strong ones get scales, and weaker ones not so much. And then he points his hands downward with palms fully open.::
Skærden... Forskarr Flottsørmir! Forskarr Pöm.<end>
::But then you begin to lose him. He describes drinking something, that you manage to catch, but the rest goes right over your head. And then he abruptly stops.::<end>
::He's waiting.::<end>
<end>
::[Intelligence] Bring your arm next to his and point out the difference. Then point to his arm and make a talking mouth with your hand.::<end>
::He stares at you.::<end>
::Point at his scales again.::<end>
::Touch his scales.:: Yes, yes. Sourmirhud.<end>
::Wait.::<end>
Come on, damn it!<end>
::Point to his scales.:: Sourmirhud. Sourmirhud.<end>
Jakke, Sørmirhud.<end>
::Point to his scales again.:: Sourmirhud, man. Tell me about sourmirhud.<end>

::He frowns.::
Sørmirhud! Ah, gäkkter!<end>
::Point to his scales angrily.:: Tell me about the goddamned sourmirhud!<end>
::Inquire about something else.::<end>
::You decide it's best to change the subject until you can figure out a way to communicate your thoughts better.::<end>

::He moves his fingers over his rough scales.::
Sørmirhud...
::Then he touches his human skin.::
Bærenhud...<end>
::Touch your skin.:: Barenhud?<end>
Jakke. Bærenhud.<end>
::Touch your skin.:: Sourmirhud?<end>
Nikke. <end>
::Point at his drawing of himself.:: Why Yngwar here?<end>

::You can see it in his eyes that he understands, but he still shakes his head.::
Nikke.<end>
::Point again.:: Why Yngwar here?<end>
Stulle, Æterbæren! Krökø!<end>
::Imitate shooing away.:: Yngwar thrown out?<end>
::Imitate fear.:: Yngwar afraid of something and ran away?<end>
::Leave it be.::<end>
::Do the drinking motion.:: Drinking, you mentioned... uh, showed you were drinking something.<end>
::He does the drinking motion alright, but everything after that is incomprehensible.::<end>
::Perhaps hearing everything in context again will help you understand what he meant better.::<end>
::Imitate drinking a potion, then point to his scales.:: Rituals. Tell me about the rituals.<end>

::He pauses, observing you intently.::
Hvæy? Hvæy græss Ik vertää ot krønn et tø Durg?<end>

::[Intelligence] You think he's asking you why he should be telling you all of this.:: You - Yngwar, great warrior. I, uh... Ik - $(context.player.Name), want become greater too. ::Gesture it as best as you can.::<end>

Durg Æterbæren bitt. Durg mætären Firg køkörr nikkt.
::He makes a lengthy pause, his eyes darting between you and the skewers.::<end>

Rit... øal. Ritøal.
Ritøal - Sørmirvääj.<end>
::[Intelligence] Observe and listen.::<end>

::He gestures drinking and shows the pain coming from below and outside. Then it subsides, and he feels much closer to the great serpents - like he's becoming one. The first ritual he describes is swimming deep, deep down, as far as possible. But the way the swimming is performed is different: His legs are tied together, his hands as well, so what he's doing is basically wriggling through the water.::
Sørmirlemen.<end>
::He seems frustrated, but you cannot figure out why. He clenches his hand into a fist ::<end>
::and again describes those men who relay Flottsørmir's messages - spiriters, but this time he's sulking.::<end>

::He drinks an imaginary potion again and begins: They are in a temple to whose waters a great serpent has been summoned. The powerful eyes of the High Spiriter can hold it in place until other spiriters can use air potions to pacify it. Then he entered its mouth and got swallowed, his arms and legs tied together. He was supposed to stay in its stomach and let its strong acid "lustrate" him and help him burn away his birthskin. But the serpent was not dazed enough and began thrashing about. Then it swam deep down with him still inside it.::<end>

::A dazed serpent cannot crush you in its stomach because its muscles get numbed, but this one squeezed him harder and harder. He undid his bonds and started crawling out. Then he saw a spear before him, a spear from one of the transcended who was hit by the serpent's tail and dropped it. He grabbed it near the tip with both of his hands as the serpent tried biting them down with its debilitated jaws - and then drove the tip through its eye...::<end>

::He emerged from the water, bathed in the serpent's acid and blood. He is a strong warrior of Flotsourmir, and he has defeated the great serpent like no Serpentborn before him has.
But the spiriters... they objected.::<end>

::He blasphemed - again. He should not be swimming with his arms free. He should not be climbing out of the water by using his legs. He should not be killing prey with tools and weapons. They told him these things before.
And he should not have used a spear - a weapon - to slay a great serpent during the ritual. After many tides he will have to abandon his arms and legs, and with them daggers and knives and spears.::<end>
Ik forskarr Flottsørmir, Yngwar forskarr Flottsørmir... met æter Sørmirbæren forskarr Flottsørmir nikkt det klögar ot Yngwar.<end>
::Yngwar was no weakling but a mighty warrior, so he was only exiled and not slain. Now he lives here alone, and he ponders...::<end>
::and describes certain people about whose purpose you aren't exactly sure.::<end>

::He drinks an imaginary potion again, and this is where you begin to lose him. The ritual involves deep waters and great serpents and ends in one's or more than one's death. But something is not right, and his sense of triumph - possibly because he is their slayer - soon diminishes.::<end>
